cases.statement: One carrier: P1 of PMID 36325013, an adult man with biopsy-proven lupus nephritis (class IV), heterozygous, inherited from his mother. The review PMID 39125844 (Table 2 row 18) summarises the same person, citing PMID 36325013 as its reference [30].

phenotype_specificity.statement: The authors state P1's presentation (adult onset, predominantly autoimmune lupus nephritis) differs from the classic early-onset autoinflammatory HA20 picture. Whole-exome sequencing was done with filtering against population databases and for dominant inheritance; no other causal variant is named. WES also found several common SLE risk alleles in P1 (Table 5), which the authors suggest may modify expressivity.

quotes.quote: Additionally, P1 was adult onset, different from previous reports.
HA20 classically presents with auto-inflammatory features.
In contrast, our patients were predominantly characterized by autoimmune features with LN.
Candidate variants were filtered to remove those presenting in the gnomAD, Kaviar, dbSNP and an in-house database and further filtered by dominant inheritance.

To explore additional factors modifying the disease phenotype, we screened the common SLE risk allele using the WES data and found that in addition to the deleterious TNFAIP3 mutation, several other common SLE risk alleles were identified in all three patients (Table 5).

segregation.statement: Inherited from the mother, who had recurrent oral ulcers. The authors state the variant co-segregated with the phenotype in the family, but the text gives no counts; relatives' genotypes are shown only in the pedigree figure (Fig. 2A-B), which is not in the text. P1's 6-year-old son had oral ulcers, duodenal ulcers and Henoch-Schönlein purpura; his genotype is not stated in the text.

quotes.quote: | Mutation origin | From mother | De novo | From mother |
The mutation co-segregated with disease phenotype in the family (Fig. 2A and B).

P1’s mother had recurrent oral ulcers, while P1’s son (6 years old) had oral ulcers; skin rashes; duodenal ulcers; anaemia; allergies to milk, egg, fish and shrimp; and had been diagnosed as Henoch–Schönlein purpura.
(B) Sanger sequencing of P1 and family members.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo: the paper states maternal origin.

quotes.quote: | Mutation origin | From mother | De novo | From mother |

functional.statement: Patient material (P1 whole-blood RNA), not a construct. RT-PCR of exon 3 to exon 7 with Sanger sequencing of cDNA, compared with one healthy control: a mutant allele with an intron 4 insertion containing a premature stop codon (p.D212Gfs*38). A20 protein level was not measured. RNA-seq of P1 whole blood showed up-regulated NF-kB signalling versus three controls and a type I IFN signature; qPCR confirmed IFN-stimulated genes; serum IL-6 raised in all three patients versus six controls.

quotes.quote: Then a set of specific primers for exon 3 and exon 7 was used to assess the effect of the splice-site variant in intron 4.
To assess mRNA splicing, we used cDNA synthesized from the proband's blood RNA and compared it with a healthy control.
Sanger sequencing of P1’s cDNA identified a mutant allele with an intron 4 insertion containing a premature stop codon resulting in p.D212Gfs*38 (Fig. 2C).
As expected, we observed significant up-regulation of NF-κB signalling compared to three controls (Fig. 4E).
A strong type I IFN signature is observed in whole blood cells of P1 compared with controls (Fig. 4F).
(I) Elevated serum cytokine IL-6 levels in the three patients (controls = 6).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice donor variant (+2 of the intron after exon 4); predicted protein p.? per the batch HGVS. The paper reports an aberrant transcript retaining intron 4 sequence, read as a frameshift p.D212Gfs*38. The paper attributes HA20 to heterozygous loss of function of TNFAIP3 and describes all three of its variants as truncating.

quotes.quote: The first mutation, c.634+2T>C,  affects the splicing of mRNA and creates a frameshift mutation that removes both the ovarian tumour (OTU) domain and all zinc finger domains.
They all lead to the truncating of the A20 protein.

Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene cause haploinsufficiency of A20 [HA20; Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) 616744], characterized by an early-onset auto-inflammatory disease [1].

computational_predictions.statement: Two splicing predictors (regSNP-splicing and HSF) reported as predicting the variant to be 'disease-causing'.

quotes.quote: In silico bioinformatics tools, including regsnp-splicing (http://regsnps-splicing.ccbb.iupui.edu/) and HSF (http://www.umd.be/HSF3/), predicted that the variant was ‘disease-causing’.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Stated absent from gnomAD, ChinaMAP, in-house controls and Infevers.

quotes.quote: All novel mutations were absent from gnomAD, ChinaMAP [14] Chinese Millionome database, in-house controls and Infevers (an online database for auto-inflammatory mutations; https://infevers.umai-montpellier.fr/web).

authors_classification.statement: The authors call the three variants, including this one, novel pathogenic and loss-of-function mutations. No ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: In summary, we report the clinical manifestations and immunological characteristics of three biopsy-proven LN patients with novel pathogenic mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene.
Novel loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 gene in patients with lupus nephritis

concerns: Protein check: the batch predicts p.? (splice site), while the papers state p.D212Gfs*38 (36325013) and Asp212Gly fs*38 (39125844). The stated protein comes from the authors' cDNA sequencing of patient RNA, not from the genomic HGVS.
Transcript not stated in either paper; the batch uses NM_001270508.2. The panel should confirm the c.634+2 numbering on that transcript.

The review (39125844) is a secondary summary of the same person (HA20-ID0220), not an independent case. Its text says the patient had allergies to milk, seafood and eggs; in the primary paper those food allergies belong to P1's son, and P1 was allergic to mould and pollen.
Carriers not in the batch: P1's mother (variant origin 'From mother'; recurrent oral ulcers). The son's genotype is shown only in Fig. 2, which is not in the text.
Other variants in the same person: WES Table 5 lists several common SLE risk alleles in P1 (e.g. C1QTNF12, PLD2, UHRF1BP1); the authors suggest they may modify the phenotype.
notes_for_panel: Single proband with maternal inheritance and RNA evidence from patient blood. The phenotype is adult-onset lupus nephritis rather than the classic Behçet-like picture; the authors state this themselves. Segregation is asserted but not counted in the text.
